questions.q: What three things does a Kubernetes RBAC rule specify?
options: Username, password, and namespace
API group, resource, and verb
Cluster name, node name, and pod name
Image name, tag, and registry
questions.explain: A rule defines what resource (like pods or secrets), in what API group, can have a given verb (get, list, watch, create, etc.) performed on it.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Role and a ClusterRole?
options: A Role can only be used by service accounts; a ClusterRole only by users
A Role is scoped to one namespace; a ClusterRole can apply cluster-wide or to cluster-scoped resources
There is no functional difference, only naming convention
A ClusterRole is deprecated in favor of Role
questions.explain: A Role's rules apply only within the namespace it's defined in, while a ClusterRole's rules can reach across every namespace or apply to resources with no namespace at all.

questions.q: What does a RoleBinding actually do?
options: It defines the list of permitted verbs for a resource
It connects a subject (user, group, or service account) to a Role's permissions
It creates a new namespace in the cluster
It deletes an existing Role
questions.explain: A Role or ClusterRole by itself is just a definition and grants nothing — the RoleBinding is what actually assigns those permissions to a specific subject.

questions.q: In the lesson's pod-reader Role example scoped to the checkout namespace, what access does it NOT grant?
options: Read access to pods in the checkout namespace
The ability to list pods in the checkout namespace
Any access to Secrets or to resources in other namespaces
The ability to watch pods in the checkout namespace
questions.explain: The Role's rules only cover the pods resource with get/list/watch verbs in the checkout namespace — it grants nothing for Secrets or other namespaces.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend namespaced Roles over ClusterRoles as the default at Northbridge Retail?
options: ClusterRoles are not supported in production clusters
Namespaced Roles enforce isolation between services sharing the cluster, avoiding unnecessary over-privileging
ClusterRoles cannot be bound to service accounts
Namespaced Roles run faster than ClusterRoles
questions.explain: Since services like checkout and inventory run in separate namespaces, namespaced Roles keep each service's access bounded to what it needs, consistent with least privilege.
